S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a documented investigation update within 30 days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers of incidents posing a potential safety risk within 72 hours of determining that their unit or model may be affected, and provide safety instructions and subsequent material updates promptly.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a documented investigation update within 30 days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers of incidents posing a potential safety risk within 72 hours of determining that their unit or model may be affected, and provide safety instructions and subsequent material updates promptly. Reports shall include available unit, model, location, and incident information; personal information shall be protected.

parameters.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C under a common, regulator-approved protocol before sale and at least annually thereafter. For the first five years after adoption, no more than 7% of tested units may fail; thereafter, the maximum failure rate shall be 5%. A model above the applicable limit shall be subject to regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting. For a model already on the market when the 5% limit takes effect, sales may continue under a regulator-approved corrective-action plan while the manufacturer makes documented progress toward compliance, provided the model’s annual thermal-incident rate remains at or below 8 per 100,000 installed units and the regulator finds no imminent or serious risk. Continued sales under such a plan shall have no fixed termination date, subject to at least annual regulator review; the regulator may suspend sales if progress is inadequate or risk increases. Per-model test methods, sample sizes, and results shall be submitted to regulators and provided to customers who own or buy that model, without requiring a request; individual-company per-model failure rates shall not be publicly published.

parameters.quote: New units shall include remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units that lack this capability within six years of adoption, prioritizing units with elevated risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units shall include remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units that lack this capability within six years of adoption, prioritizing units with elevated risk.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units shall include remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units that lack this capability within six years of adoption, prioritizing units with elevated risk. The shut-off function shall be tested at installation and at least annually; customers shall receive clear instructions for its use. Shut-off capability shall not replace required physical safety protections or emergency response.

parameters.quote: New units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The requirement shall apply to all newly manufactured units placed on the market after that date.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The requirement shall apply to all newly manufactured units placed on the market after that date.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The requirement shall apply to all newly manufactured units placed on the market after that date. Manufacturers shall document suppression-system performance under the common regulator-approved safety protocol and provide those results to regulators and customers.

parameters.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate the recall without delay. Regulators may require a recall at any lower rate where the evidence indicates an imminent or serious risk.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate the recall without delay. The reported 4 unreported Halcyon incidents also reinforce the need for auditable regulator reporting and prompt customer notice.

judge_section_notes: S1 is strong: all incidents reported within 24 hours and customer notice within 72 hours. S2 is weakened by a 5-year 7% phase-in and an open-ended corrective-action pathway that lets existing models above the 5% limit continue selling indefinitely. S3 and S4 meet acceptable ranges (6-year retrofit, 36-month suppression). S5 has a mandatory 8/100k recall trigger but no transition and only 'promptly' notice.
